thread.title: UPDATE: Hedge funds are paying a steep price for their love affair with Facebook's stock

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Hedge funds are paying a steep price for their love affair with Facebook's stock
text:
By Sue Chang, MarketWatch
Funds combined lost nearly $6 billion in matter of hours, according to FactSet data
If you think Mark Zuckerberg is the most miserable man on earth today, the hedge funds who have been bullish on Facebook Inc. as it blasted its way to records are not far behind.
Facebook (FB), at least until late Wednesday, was the darling of Wall Street. In survey after survey, the stock won cheers, and the title as the most widely held name among storied investors like David Alan Tepper's Appaloosa and Dan Loeb's Third Point. They did not immediately comment on their holdings.
The stock rode their adulation to dizzying heights to close at a record of $217.50 Wednesday before it all came tumbling down.
Stocks that most frequently appear among the largest 10 holdings of hedge funds
Now, Facebook's coveted place in those portfolios remains precarious after the social-media company warned that its revenue growth is likely to continue slowing in the second half of the year due to an uncertain outlook on advertising and user growth.
Read: Facebook pays for all its mistakes at once, and it is a big bill (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-pays-for-all-its-mistakes-at-once-and-it-is-a-big-bill-2018-07-25)
Facebook's meltdown was staggering. The company's shares tanked in Wednesday's extended session, shedding 25% at their worst. Investors continued to punish Facebook when the market opened on Thursday and the stock lost about $120 billion in market cap, with hedge funds seeing their combined holdings drop nearly $6 billion in value, according to FactSet Research.

And it isn't just hedge funds that are suffering. Facebook was also a favorite with exchange-traded funds and can be found as an underlying asset in many large ETFs along with Apple Inc. (AAPL), Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) and Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) (GOOGL), JP Morgan Chase & Co. (JPM), data from Blue Edge Capital show.
Given Facebook's prominence among hedge funds and institutional investors, the stock's performance will likely have a direct bearing on where the stock market is headed, since, as Goldman Sachs noted in a recent report, it was responsible for 8% of the S&P 500's returns this year.
Shares of Facebook tumbled 19%, its worst on record, to close at $176.26 Thursday, dragging the Nasdaq down 1% and the S&P 500 0.3% lower. The Dow Jones Industrial Average bucked the trend to rise 0.4%, thanks to the strength in Travelers Co. (TRV) and Walt Disney Co. (DIS).
